features.name: own_career_milestone
features.question: Does the post announce a change or milestone in the author's own career, such as a new job, promotion, work anniversary, or leaving a role?
features.definition: The author reports a change or milestone in their own job or career path.
features.yes_example: After four years at the clinic, today is my last day.
features.no_example: Our team shipped the new billing module this week.
features.hypothesis: Career news invites congratulations from the author's network.

features.name: celebrates_someone_else
features.question: Is the post mainly about celebrating an achievement of a person or team other than the author?
features.definition: The main subject is another person's or team's success, award, or milestone, not the author's own.
features.yes_example: Huge congratulations to Priya on defending her PhD today!
features.no_example: I just defended my PhD today.
features.hypothesis: Separates celebrating others from self-promotion; both may lift reactions differently.

features.name: admits_own_mistake
features.question: Does the author describe a mistake or failure they personally made?
features.definition: The author admits an error, wrong decision, or failure of their own.
features.yes_example: I hired too fast and it cost us the team.
features.no_example: Many founders hire too fast.
features.hypothesis: Vulnerability is common LinkedIn advice; test it.

features.name: personal_life_outside_work
features.question: Does the post mention the author's life outside work, such as family, health, or hobbies?
features.definition: The post refers to the author's family, health, home life, or personal interests beyond their job.
features.yes_example: My daughter asked me what I do all day.
features.no_example: Our quarterly numbers came in today.
features.hypothesis: Personal context may humanize the author.

features.name: describes_hardship
features.question: Does the post describe a hardship such as illness, loss, layoff, or burnout that affected the author or people close to them?
features.definition: The author recounts a difficult life or career event affecting themselves or someone close.
features.yes_example: Last year I was laid off two weeks before my wedding.
features.no_example: Layoffs are rising across the tech sector.
features.hypothesis: Hardship stories draw support.

features.name: asks_for_personal_help
features.question: Does the author ask readers for help for themselves, such as referrals, a job, or introductions?
features.definition: The post requests personal help, a job lead, or an introduction for the author.
features.yes_example: If you know a team hiring product designers, I would love an intro.
features.no_example: We are hiring product designers, apply here.
features.hypothesis: Requests for help mobilize the network.

features.name: welcomes_new_member
features.question: Does the post welcome a new person to a team, company, or group?
features.definition: The post introduces and welcomes a newly joined colleague, member, or partner.
features.yes_example: Please welcome Tom, who joins our design team today.
features.no_example: Tom has led our design team for five years.
features.hypothesis: Welcomes are people-centered like thanks.

features.name: farewell
features.question: Does the post say goodbye to a role, team, place, or person?
features.definition: The author marks leaving or the departure of someone or something with a farewell.
features.yes_example: Saying goodbye to the team that taught me everything.
features.no_example: Excited to start my new role on Monday.
features.hypothesis: Farewells collect goodwill.

features.name: names_three_plus_people
features.question: Does the post name three or more specific people?
features.definition: At least three distinct individuals are named in the post.
features.yes_example: Thanks to Ana, Ben, and Chloe for making this happen.
features.no_example: Thanks to the whole team for making this happen.
features.hypothesis: Naming people may bring those people and their networks in.

features.name: opens_in_a_specific_moment
features.question: Does the first sentence place the reader in a specific moment, giving a time, place, or action that happened?
features.definition: The opening sentence describes a concrete scene or moment rather than a general statement.
features.yes_example: At 6am on Tuesday, my phone buzzed with a message from our biggest client.
features.no_example: Client communication is the key to growth.
features.hypothesis: Scene openings are common hook advice; test it.

features.name: opens_with_bold_claim
features.question: Does the first sentence state a firm opinion or claim on its own line?
features.definition: The post opens with a one-sentence assertion of the author's view, set apart from what follows.
features.yes_example: Cold outreach is dead.
features.no_example: I have been thinking about outreach lately and wanted to share some notes.
features.hypothesis: Bold one-line hooks are common advice; test it.

features.name: organization_voice
features.question: Is the post written as an organization speaking, rather than as an individual person?
features.definition: The post speaks as a company or institution (official announcement style) with no individual's perspective.
features.yes_example: Acme Corp is pleased to announce our new partnership with Beta Ltd.
features.no_example: I am so excited that we are partnering with Beta Ltd.
features.hypothesis: Official-sounding posts may underperform personal ones.

features.name: generic_advice_without_experience
features.question: Does the post give advice without tying it to anything the author experienced or did?
features.definition: The post offers tips or guidance stated in general terms, with no event from the author's own experience.
features.yes_example: Five tips to improve your resume: keep it to one page...
features.no_example: When I rewrote my resume last year, cutting it to one page got me three interviews.
features.hypothesis: Advice underperforms in the data; check whether personal grounding removes the penalty.

features.name: engagement_bait
features.question: Does the post ask readers to comment a word, like, or share in order to receive something?
features.definition: Readers are told to comment a keyword, react, or repost to get a resource or reward.
features.yes_example: Comment 'GUIDE' and I'll send you the template.
features.no_example: Here is the template, link below.
features.hypothesis: Comment-for-resource tactics may raise reactions.

features.name: behind_the_scenes
features.question: Does the post show how the author's own work or organization operates internally?
features.definition: The post reveals internal processes, routines, or moments not normally visible from outside.
features.yes_example: Here is what our Monday planning meeting actually looks like.
features.no_example: Our product helps teams plan faster.
features.hypothesis: Insider views may attract curiosity.

features.name: admits_doubt_or_fear
features.question: Does the author say they felt doubt, fear, or insecurity?
features.definition: The author states a personal feeling of doubt, fear, nervousness, or insecurity.
features.yes_example: Honestly, I was terrified before going on stage.
features.no_example: The talk went well and the audience was great.
features.hypothesis: Emotional vulnerability is a specific emotion beyond general emotion.

features.name: reports_own_numeric_result
features.question: Does the post report a numeric result the author or their team achieved?
features.definition: The post gives a number that measures an outcome the author or their team accomplished.
features.yes_example: We grew from 3 to 40 customers in six months.
features.no_example: Most startups take years to find customers.
features.hypothesis: Concrete own results may be more credible than general statistics.

features.name: mentions_duration_of_journey
features.question: Does the post state how long the author has spent on something, such as years in a field or months on a project?
features.definition: The post gives a length of time the author has invested in a career, project, or goal.
features.yes_example: Ten years ago I wrote my first line of code.
features.no_example: I wrote some code this weekend.
features.hypothesis: Journey framing signals a milestone.

features.name: reports_company_shutdown
features.question: Does the post report that a named company is shutting down, laying off staff, or ceasing operations?
features.definition: The post states that a specific company has closed, is closing, or is cutting most of its workforce.
features.yes_example: Acme Corp is shutting down and laying off 200 employees.
features.no_example: Acme Corp launched a new product line today.
features.hypothesis: I expect posts about company shutdowns to get more reactions.

features.name: advertises_remote_job
features.question: Does the post advertise a job position that is explicitly described as remote?
features.definition: The post lists an open job and states that the work can be done remotely, without requiring a specific office location.
features.yes_example: Hiring: Remote Frontend Developer. Work from anywhere.
features.no_example: Hiring: Frontend Developer in San Francisco.
features.hypothesis: I expect remote job ads to get more reactions than onsite ones.

features.name: gives_numeric_breakdown
features.question: Does the post break down a total amount into component parts, showing how the parts sum to the total?
features.definition: The post presents a total figure and then lists at least two component amounts that add up to that total.
features.yes_example: Total cost: $1,000. Materials: $600. Labor: $300. Overhead: $100.
features.no_example: The project cost $1,000, including materials and labor.
features.hypothesis: I expect numeric breakdowns to increase engagement.

features.name: names_rejecting_organization
features.question: Does the post explicitly name a company or organization that rejected or failed the author?
features.definition: The post describes a negative outcome experienced by the author and names the specific company or organization responsible.
features.yes_example: Acme Inc. rejected me after three interviews.
features.no_example: I was rejected after three interviews.
features.hypothesis: I expect posts that name the rejecting organization to get more reactions.

features.name: asks_for_likes_or_shares
features.question: Does the post explicitly ask readers to like, share, or repost the content?
features.definition: Yes if the post contains a direct request for the reader to like, share, repost, or forward the post itself.
features.yes_example: Please like and share this post with your network if you agree.
features.no_example: I hope this helps you.
features.hypothesis: Explicit engagement requests prompt more reactions.

features.name: mentions_animals
features.question: Does the post mention a non-human animal, either literally or as a prominent image?
features.definition: Yes if the post references animals, pets, or uses animal-related imagery such as dogs or cats as a notable element.
features.yes_example: Meet our office puppy who makes every standup better.
features.no_example: We shipped a new feature for analytics dashboards.
features.hypothesis: Animal content triggers positive emotions and sharing.

features.name: discusses_mortality
features.question: Does the post explicitly discuss death, dying, or mortality as a central theme?
features.definition: Yes if the post addresses the topic of death, human mortality, or the inevitability of dying.
features.yes_example: Remembering that we are mortal can clarify what truly matters in work and life.
features.no_example: Our new product launch exceeded all expectations.
features.hypothesis: Mortality themes provoke deep reflection and resonance.

features.name: describes_company_conflict
features.question: Does the post report or analyze a conflict, dispute, or competitive tension between two or more named companies?
features.definition: Yes if the post describes a specific clash, lawsuit, suspension of partnership, or other antagonistic action involving identifiable organizations.
features.yes_example: Acme Corp has cut off integration access for Beta Inc, citing competitive concerns.
features.no_example: Both companies are seeing strong growth in the cloud market.
features.hypothesis: Conflict narratives drive attention and discussion.

features.name: offers_free_resource
features.question: Does the post offer the reader something for free, such as a resource, tool, audit, trial, or download?
features.definition: The post states that the reader can obtain a named item or service at no cost.
features.yes_example: Get my free checklist for launching your first product.
features.no_example: Our new paid course is now open for enrollment.
features.hypothesis: Posts offering a free resource generate more reactions because readers respond to tangible no-cost value.

features.name: uses_negative_emotion_language
features.question: Does the post use strongly negative emotional language to describe a situation, practice, or trend?
features.definition: Yes if the post includes at least one vivid negative emotion word or metaphor that conveys distress, exploitation, or outrage.
features.yes_example: This exploitative practice is humiliating skilled professionals and harvesting their knowledge.
features.no_example: The company announced a new policy update today.
features.hypothesis: Strong negative emotion prompts strong reactions.

features.name: states_new_initiative_proposal
features.question: Does the post propose the creation of a new initiative, fund, program, or organization that does not currently exist?
features.definition: Yes if the author advocates for establishing something new to address a problem or opportunity, beyond just recommending a practice.
features.yes_example: We need a global fund to support early-stage climate tech startups.
features.no_example: Adopting agile methods can improve team efficiency.
features.hypothesis: Proposing concrete new ideas sparks discussion and support.

features.name: announces_personal_life_milestone_outside_work
features.question: Does the post announce a personal life event outside work, such as a new child, marriage, anniversary, or relocation?
features.definition: Yes when the author explicitly shares a non-work life event or milestone about themselves or their family.
features.yes_example: We just brought home baby number three!
features.no_example: Three tips for better LP introductions.
features.hypothesis: Personal life milestone posts tend to get more reactions than purely professional content.

features.name: announces_career_change_or_open_to_new_roles
features.question: Does the post state that the author is leaving a previous role, starting a new role, or now available for work?
features.definition: Yes when the author explicitly announces a job change, departure, or new availability for opportunities.
features.yes_example: Yesterday was my last day at NetNut. Now open for fractional work.
features.no_example: I want work that combines passion, impact, and income.
features.hypothesis: Career change or availability announcements tend to get more reactions than general musings about work.

features.name: uses_vivid_sensory_imagery
features.question: Does the post include at least one adjective describing a color, temperature, or weather condition used figuratively or for atmosphere?
features.definition: Yes when the text uses sensory color, temperature, or weather words beyond literal description to create a mood.
features.yes_example: The celadon skies and melting tarmac greeted us.
features.no_example: The event is full and includes breakfast.
features.hypothesis: Vivid sensory imagery tends to get more reactions than straightforward descriptions.

features.name: named_company_metric
features.question: Does the post mention a specific named company and at least one quantified operational result, such as a percentage time or cost change?
features.definition: Yes when the post gives a numeric business outcome for a named company or product.
features.yes_example: Hyundai cut crash-safety review time by 90%.
features.no_example: AI can help you build faster.
features.hypothesis: Named-company quantified results lend credibility and shareability.

features.name: describes_grant_or_funding_opportunity
features.question: Does the post describe a grant, award, or non-job funding opportunity for organizations or individuals?
features.definition: Yes when the main subject is a grant or award with an application process, not a paid job opening.
features.yes_example: Apply for a $2,000 bee education grant by October 31.
features.no_example: We are hiring an economic analyst in Accra.
features.hypothesis: Grant opportunity posts tend to get more reactions than job openings from the same account.

features.name: calls_out_hiring_discrimination
features.question: Does the post describe a specific incident where a person was treated unfairly because of nationality, gender, age, or another protected characteristic?
features.definition: Yes when the post recounts an employment decision explicitly based on nationality, gender, age, or another protected characteristic.
features.yes_example: The manager said, 'We prefer people from certain countries.'
features.no_example: Performance reviews can be misleading.
features.hypothesis: Posts calling out specific discriminatory hiring practices tend to get more reactions than generic HR criticism.

features.name: previews_interview_with_specific_topic_list
features.question: Does the post preview a podcast or interview by listing at least three specific discussion topics or questions?
features.definition: Yes when the post enumerates several concrete conversation points from an interview before releasing it.
features.yes_example: We discussed: lessons from bankruptcy, relationship building, and why asking for help matters.
features.no_example: Enjoyed the conversation; episode coming soon.
features.hypothesis: Posts that preview an interview with a specific topic list tend to get more reactions than vague gratitude.

features.name: contains_standalone_aphorism
features.question: Does the post contain a standalone, pithy one-sentence statement of a general principle or truth that could be quoted independently?
features.definition: Yes if there is a short, memorable sentence stating a universal rule or observation, separate from the main narrative.
features.yes_example: Business is simple: do what you said you'd do.
features.no_example: We are building an AI system that continuously advances work.
features.hypothesis: Standalone aphorisms are highly shareable and quotable.

features.name: promises_future_how_to
features.question: Does the post promise to share a step-by-step process or tutorial in a future post?
features.definition: Yes if the author explicitly says they will later provide detailed instructions or a walkthrough of a method.
features.yes_example: In my next post, I'll walk you through how I built it.
features.no_example: Here is what I learned from my experience.
features.hypothesis: Promising a future how-to creates anticipation and book readers for follow-up.

features.name: uses_nickname_for_public_figure
features.question: Does the post refer to a public figure by an informal nickname, first name only, or playful label rather than a formal title?
features.definition: Yes if the post uses a casual or humorous name for a well-known person instead of their official or full name.
features.yes_example: The Don is at it again with tariffs.
features.no_example: President Trump announced new tariffs.
features.hypothesis: Informal nicknames signal insider personality and humor.

features.name: presents_multiple_distinct_case_examples
features.question: Does the post present at least two separate, distinct case examples or user stories to illustrate its point?
features.definition: Yes if the post includes two or more independent narratives or examples of different people or situations.
features.yes_example: A veteran asks about benefits; a cancer patient uses AI to understand treatment.
features.no_example: One patient used AI to understand her diagnosis.
features.hypothesis: Multiple distinct case examples show broader relevance and richer content.

features.name: opens_with_named_entity
features.question: Does the first sentence of the post mention a specific named company, product, or person as its main subject?
features.definition: Answer yes when the opening sentence identifies a particular brand, organization, product, or individual.
features.yes_example: Stripe just announced a new AI gateway for startups.
features.no_example: The best advice I ever received came from a mentor.
features.hypothesis: Opening with a concrete named entity increases immediate relevance and curiosity.

features.name: framed_as_takeaways_from_source
features.question: Does the post explicitly frame its content as takeaways or lessons from a specific source, such as an interview, event, or named person?
features.definition: Answer yes when the post states that it will share insights, lessons, or takeaways derived from a named person, event, or source.
features.yes_example: Five lessons I learned from interviewing a successful founder.
features.no_example: Here are some thoughts about startup growth.
features.hypothesis: Posts that promise curated takeaways from a specific source attract readers seeking distilled wisdom.

features.name: tags_multiple_individuals
features.question: Does the post mention or tag at least two specific individuals by name, either in the body text or in a list of tags?
features.definition: Answer yes when the post names two or more distinct persons, excluding hashtags.
features.yes_example: Thanks to Alice Johnson and Bob Lee for collaborating on this project.
features.no_example: Had a useful meeting with a potential partner yesterday.
features.hypothesis: Mentioning multiple specific people can notify them and expand the post's reach.

features.name: mentions_limited_quantity
features.question: Does the post specify a numerical limit on the number of people who can take advantage of an offer or opportunity?
features.definition: Answer yes when the post states a cap on participants, spots, or items, such as 'only 30 founders' or '5 slots'.
features.yes_example: We have only three slots left for the workshop.
features.no_example: Register for the workshop at the link below.
features.hypothesis: Explicit numeric scarcity increases perceived value and urgency.

features.name: casual_opening_greeting
features.question: Does the post open with a casual greeting, apology, or informal conversational opener directed at the reader?
features.definition: Yes when the first sentence is a friendly greeting, apology for absence, or informal remark to the reader.
features.yes_example: Hey everyone, sorry I've been quiet this week.
features.no_example: We are hiring a data engineer.
features.hypothesis: Casual openers create a personal, approachable tone and may increase reactions.

features.name: resource_list_opportunities
features.question: Does the post list multiple external opportunities such as grants, funding programs, scholarships, or similar that the reader can apply to?
features.definition: Yes when the post enumerates two or more named opportunities with eligibility or application details for the reader.
features.yes_example: Here are three grants: Startup India Seed Fund, NIDHI PRAYAS, and BIRAC BIG.
features.no_example: This year saw a shift in D2C funding patterns.
features.hypothesis: Resource list posts outperform general analysis because they offer direct utility.
